items.title: 67425_Tiny Grimes oral history interview
items.q: You made a lot of records with those guys -- Red Prysock and Screamin' Jay.

ctx.x: Oh, Now you're talkin' entertainment, these guys -- well that's what they need, They need something and they really appreciate it. It's no problem. Everything is nice, you know. You can even get to hang out to a certain extent. I know quite a few fellas up there, you know. So, I'll be glad to do it. I got the personnel, it's just a matter of what the date is going be. I don't even know what the name of the prison -- I think it's Raybrook.
So, you said you played in Cleveland for a while, and then you went to Detroit and traveled around a bit -- Canada -- but you did end up in Philadelphia for quite some time too.
Oh yeah, well I was in Chicago, too, for a while, and when I hit Philadelphia --

items.title: 67425_Tiny Grimes oral history interview
items.q: Screamin' Jay Hawkins had just got out of the airforce, I believe -- or navy or somethin'. And he kept askin' me for a job -- I didn't have no room for another fella

ctx.x: Cleveland Ohio. I went there for two weeks, stayed 2 years. And I discovered quite a few fellas, you know... Sonny Payne, I had to ask his mother, could he come out on the road, after I found out he could play. And his father was in

Chis Columbo down in Atlantic City. And they let him go out. I had to ask another fella's mother could he go out, Ray Bryant, but I heard him play, and said this cat sure could play -- young kid, you know, he couldn't go, so I had to ask his mother could he go. She ok'd it. Red Prysock had just got out of the army or navy or somethin', and... But those are some of the fellas that I helped get started in a way of speakin'. Screamin' Jay Hawkins had just got out of the airforce, I believe -- or navy or somethin'.…
Did you make any records with him?
